Landing.faqA1: In gasless mode, customers don't need POL or ETH — they pay with just their JPYC or USDC balance (that's what "gasless" means here). For JPYC gasless payments, a per-transaction OpenPay usage fee applies (1% of the payment with a 2 JPYC minimum), deducted at settlement and split to OpenPay's designated wallet within the same transaction (the principal price of goods still transfers directly from the customer's wallet to the merchant's wallet; OpenPay does not hold sales). The store bears the fee, so the customer pays only the displayed amount and the merchant's net amount is the payment less the fee (the customer simply signs the transfer in JPYC). For tips to creators, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC; the 1% does not apply) is borne by the customer sending the tip. For USDC payments, the customer pays gas in USDC to the paymaster, so OpenPay does not collect a gas-equivalent (USDC gasless requires an EIP-7702-capable smart-account wallet; ordinary wallets fall back to standard payment where the customer pays their own gas — JPYC gasless works with any wallet). Cross-chain payments (paying from a different source chain) are not gasless — the source chain's network fee (ETH/POL etc.) is paid by the customer.
Landing.faqQ2: Can I receive both JPYC and USDC?
Landing.faqA2: Both are supported: JPYC for JPY-denominated receipts, USDC for Web3 or international customers. JPYC supports Polygon / Kaia / Avalanche / Ethereum (standard mode only on Ethereum); USDC supports Base / Arbitrum / Optimism / Polygon / Ethereum / Avalanche. Choose in the QR builder; Circle CCTP V2 handles other source chains.
Landing.faqQ3: What if the customer has no wallet?
Landing.faqA3: Recommend MetaMask or Rabby on desktop, and HashPort Wallet / Myna Wallet / MetaMask Mobile on phones. Multiple wallets are detected automatically.
Landing.faqQ4: How do I convert JPYC / USDC to JPY?
Landing.faqA4: Redeem JPYC 1:1 at <jpycEx>JPYC EX</jpycEx>, or sell USDC via SBI VC Trade and other Japanese exchanges. Links are on the <create>Receive</create> page.
Landing.faqA5: History stays in browser LocalStorage, not on OpenPay servers. Export CSV or verify recorded transaction hashes on Etherscan / Polygonscan.
Landing.faqA6: The OpenPay usage fee. For JPYC gasless payments (where the Company sponsors the gas), a per-transaction OpenPay usage fee applies (1% of the payment with a 2 JPYC minimum), deducted at settlement and split to OpenPay's designated wallet within the same transaction (the principal price of goods is sent directly to the merchant's wallet; OpenPay does not hold sales). The store bears this fee, and the customer pays only the displayed amount (for tips to creators, the gas-equivalent amount — about 2 JPYC; the 1% does not apply — is borne by the customer sending the tip). Paths where the customer pays gas themselves (e.g. USDC), and Standard (with-gas) payments, are not in scope (free). Note: if you use the mobile-order feature (in-store/kiosk and pre-order mobile ordering), the OpenPay usage fee is charged at a different rate — the mobile-order system fee (1% of the payment for in-store/kiosk; 3% for pre-order, gas included) — applied instead of, not in addition to, the gasless usage fee, regardless of the payment path (for pre-order, either store-borne or added to the customer total depending on the store setting). See the Terms of Service and the Specified Commercial Transactions Act disclosure for details.
Landing.faqA7: Both are blockchain-based stablecoins. JPYC tracks the yen (1 JPYC ≈ 1 JPY); Circle’s USDC tracks the dollar (1 USDC ≈ 1 USD), reducing payment-price volatility.
Landing.faqQ8: Can I use OpenPay for business invoices such as development or maintenance fees?
Landing.faqA8: Yes. Beyond in-store QR payments, you can request development fees, production fees, or monthly maintenance fees. Send a payment link with the amount and funds settle directly to your wallet, with accounting CSV and e-receipts for your records.

gasHint.title: When you have no gas (POL / ETH) to send tokens to an exchange
gasHint.body: Sending received JPYC / USDC to an exchange requires a small amount of native gas on each chain (POL on Polygon, ETH on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism). With MetaMask's Swap (Gas Station) feature, you can swap on Polygon / Base / Arbitrum without holding any POL or ETH — the gas fee is paid out of your JPYC or USDC. On chains where Gas Station is not available (e.g. Optimism), a small amount of ETH is required separately to initiate the swap.
gasHint.disclaimer: Note: Availability, supported chains, and success of MetaMask features depend on MetaMask itself; OpenPay is not involved. Network congestion or unsupported token routes on any chain may cause the swap to fail.

Terms.intro: These Terms of Service (the "Terms") govern your use of the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service") operated by {company} (the "Company"). By using the Service, you agree to be bound by these Terms.

article1.title: Article 1 (Application)
article1.body: These Terms apply to all relationships between users and the Company concerning the use of the Service. If the Company separately establishes individual rules on the Service, such individual rules form part of these Terms; in case of conflict, individual rules prevail.

article2.title: Article 2 (Definitions)
article2.body: (1) "Merchant" means a business or individual who receives Supported Token payments through the Service. (2) "Customer" means a person who pays a Merchant through the Service. (3) "Wallet" means a self-custodial crypto wallet (EOA or smart contract account) controlled by the user. (4) "Supported Token" means a digital asset supported by the Service, currently including JPYC, an electronic payment instrument issued by JPYC Inc. as a funds transfer service provider registered under Japan's Payment Services Act, and USDC, a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, Inc. (5) "Network Fee" means gas required to confirm a blockchain transaction. (6) "Gasless Payment" means a payment mode in which the Customer can complete payment without separately holding a native token (POL, ETH, etc.), and includes (a) paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee using an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar (e.g. JPYC payments), and (b) paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token via an ERC-4337 ERC20 Paymaster (e.g. USDC payments). (7) "Standard Payment (with Gas)" means a payment mode in which the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee and the Customer pays it from their own wallet.

article3.title: Article 3 (Nature of the Service)
article3.body: The Service is a non-custodial tool that facilitates transfers of Supported Tokens between user wallets. The Company never holds user funds. All transfers are executed on-chain via the user's own signature. The Company does not issue or operate the Supported Tokens, the underlying blockchains, or the wallet applications used by users. The Service consists of generating EIP-681 payment URIs, QR codes, batching user operations under the ERC-4337 standard, and relaying gas sponsorship; the Company does not intermediate in the underlying user-to-user transaction itself. The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds payable from Customer to Merchant. In a payment through the Service, the price of goods and similar amounts are transferred directly from the Customer's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet. Separately, in Gasless Payment paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) via an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar, or via an EIP-3009 technical relay (JPYC payments), the Company charges a per-transaction usage fee (the "OpenPay usage fee") to Merchants who use JPYC gasless payments, as consideration for use of the Service. The OpenPay usage fee is 1% (10 per 1,000) of the payment with a minimum of 2 JPYC. The OpenPay usage fee is taken at the time each payment is executed (at on-chain settlement), split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. The OpenPay usage fee is borne by the Merchant (the Customer pays only the displayed payment amount, and the fee is deducted from the amount the Merchant receives); the net amount the Merchant receives is the payment amount less the OpenPay usage fee. For tips to creators, however, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC per transaction; the 1% of the payment does not apply) is borne by the Customer sending the tip (only in this case does the Customer add the gas-equivalent amount on top of the tip). The OpenPay usage fee is consideration for use of the Service, not for the purpose of recovering gas, and is not linked to the actual gas amount. The Company receives only the OpenPay usage fee portion; the principal price of goods and similar amounts (excluding the OpenPay usage fee) is transferred directly from the Customer's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet. In paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company. No OpenPay usage fee arises for the act of receiving a payment itself, for use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, or for paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC). However, for JPYC payments checked out via the register (in-store POS) feature, from the July 2026 usage period the same OpenPay usage fee as gasless (1% of the payment) is charged as consideration for use of the Service (the register and other payment systems), even in Standard (with-gas) mode (deducted from the merchant's receipt; the customer still pays their own gas). Payment QR (/pay), tips to creators, the USDC route, and manually created payment links remain out of scope (free). For transactions made in Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays it from their own wallet. The handling of gas in any of the above paths is a feature of the Service and does not constitute custody or management of user assets by the Company.

article4.title: Article 4 (Usage Environment)
article4.body: Users are responsible for preparing, at their own cost and risk, a compatible wallet, internet connection, token balance, and (when using Standard Payment (with Gas) mode or any other path where the Company does not sponsor gas) gas in the native token. Supported chains and tokens may be added, changed, or suspended at the Company's discretion without prior notice. In addition, users must have the legal capacity required to use the Service. Minors may use the Service only with the consent of a parent or other legal representative.

article5.title: Article 5 (Fees)
article5.body: (1) The Company provides payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, amount/token/network selection, supported wallet integration, gas sponsorship and payment relay in the Gasless Payment mode, and operation and maintenance of the Service. The Company charges a per-transaction usage fee (the "OpenPay usage fee") to Merchants who make JPYC gasless payments using the Service (in particular, gas sponsorship and payment relay in the Gasless Payment mode), as consideration for use of the Service. The OpenPay usage fee is 1% (10 per 1,000) of the payment with a minimum of 2 JPYC (the fee is triggered by JPYC gasless usage; paths where the Customer pays gas themselves—e.g. USDC via the ERC20 Paymaster—are not in scope). The OpenPay usage fee is taken, as consideration for use of the Service, at the time each payment is executed (at on-chain settlement), split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. The OpenPay usage fee is borne by the Merchant (the Customer pays only the displayed payment amount, and the fee is deducted from the amount the Merchant receives); the net amount the Merchant receives is the payment amount less the OpenPay usage fee. For tips to creators, however, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC per transaction; the 1% of the payment does not apply) is borne by the Customer sending the tip (only in this case does the Customer add the gas-equivalent amount on top of the tip). The Company receives only the OpenPay usage fee portion; the principal price of goods and similar amounts continues to be transferred directly to the Merchant's designated wallet. The act of receiving a payment itself and the use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode are free. (2) In Gasless Payment paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) via an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar, or via an EIP-3009 technical relay (e.g. JPYC payments), the Company sponsors that Network Fee and charges the OpenPay usage fee under (1) (the OpenPay usage fee is consideration for use of the Service, not for the purpose of recovering gas, and is not linked to the actual gas amount). The principal price of goods and similar amounts (excluding the OpenPay usage fee) is transferred directly to the Merchant's designated wallet. In paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and the Company does not collect it (no OpenPay usage fee arises for this path). (3) In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays the Network Fee in the native token from their own wallet, and no OpenPay usage fee arises for this path. However, for JPYC payments checked out via the register (in-store POS) feature, from the July 2026 usage period the same OpenPay usage fee as gasless (1% of the payment) is charged as consideration for use of the Service (the register and other payment systems), even in Standard (with-gas) mode (deducted from the merchant's receipt; the customer still pays their own gas). Payment QR (/pay), tips to creators, the USDC route, and manually created payment links remain out of scope (free). (4) Payments through the Service are sent on-chain directly from the user's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet (for JPYC gasless payments, only the OpenPay usage fee portion is split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction). The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds (excluding the OpenPay usage fee) payable from Customer to Merchant, and there is no mechanism for the Company to deduct from Merchant sales proceeds or to pre-charge. (5) The fee schedule, the rate, calculation method, and collection method of the OpenPay usage fee, the supported tokens, supported chains, payment modes, and the availability and conditions of gas sponsorship may be changed at the Company's discretion. If the Company changes the OpenPay usage fee, it will give prior notice of its content and the effective time in the manner provided in these Terms and apply it to use on or after the effective time. The OpenPay usage fee is taken at settlement within the same transaction; if for any reason the Company cannot collect the OpenPay usage fee from a Merchant, the Company may suspend gasless payment relay for that Merchant (the act of receiving a payment itself and the use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode remain available). (6) For a Supported Token, if a method with a clearer network-fee structure becomes available (such as a native paymaster for that token), the Company may migrate the technical method of gas sponsorship to that method. (7) For the accounting CSV download feature, after this feature is enabled the Company may offer a separate optional right to use, the "CSV 24-hour pass" (100 JPYC per purchase, valid for 24 hours from the time of payment). The CSV pass is prepaid; viewing your transaction history and the act of receiving payments themselves remain free. The CSV pass is non-refundable (no refunds or prorated refunds after payment) and does not auto-renew. Re-purchasing grants 24 hours from the new payment time and does not stack onto any remaining time, and paying more than 100 JPYC still grants only 24 hours of validity. Where available in your environment, paying for the CSV pass defaults to gasless purchase (sign only; the Company bears the Network Fee (gas) required to send it). If you choose the path of buying by sending with gas, the Network Fee (gas) for that transfer is borne by the user. The Company will announce when this feature becomes available within the Service. (8) If you use the mobile-order feature (in-store / kiosk ordering and pre-order mobile ordering), the Company applies a different rate of the OpenPay usage fee for use of the mobile-order feature (including the shop page, menu, order management, and order relay): it does not charge this in addition to the gasless usage fee above, but applies only the following rate (this rate is the mobile-order system fee; where the Company sponsors gas for a gasless mobile order, that gas is included in this rate, and the gasless usage fee above is not charged again on top). This fee is charged per mobile-order payment regardless of the payment path (whether gasless or standard, and therefore even for standard payments where the Customer pays the Network Fee themselves); the rate is 1% of the payment for in-store/kiosk and 3% for pre-order mobile ordering. For pre-order mobile ordering, depending on the store setting, either the store bears the fee out of the amount it receives (the Customer pays only the price of goods) or the Customer pays it on top of the price of goods. In either case the principal price of goods is transferred directly to the Merchant's designated wallet (the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales), and only the fee portion is split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. This mobile-order system fee was introduced on June 17, 2026 and applies to use of the mobile-order feature on and after the day the feature becomes available; /pay payment links, tips to creators, and standard payment links other than mobile order are not in scope. The fee is added on the buyer's side (the payer) on top of the listed price (the seller—i.e., the resource registrant—receives the listed price in full), and is split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction at the time each payment is executed (on-chain settlement). The principal price is transferred directly to the seller's designated wallet, and the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales (non-custodial). Network fees (gas) the Company sponsors for gasless settlement of the x402 facilitator are included in this fee. This x402 facilitator fee was newly established on June 28, 2026; it is a separate consideration, independent of the OpenPay usage fee (gasless payments, etc.) and the mobile-order system fee above (only this fee applies to x402 payments, with no duplication). /pay payment links, tips to creators, in-store payments, and mobile ordering are not subject to this x402 facilitator fee. Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: {company} (the "Company") establishes this Privacy Policy (the "Policy") regarding the handling of personal information in connection with the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service"), in compliance with the Act on the Protection of Personal Information of Japan (the "APPI") and related laws.

section1.title: 1. Information We Collect
section1.body: We collect the following information in connection with the Service: (1) blockchain wallet addresses that the Company observes when users connect their wallet to the Service; (2) server log information including browser information, IP address, referrer, access timestamps, and page navigation; (3) anonymized statistics collected by Vercel Analytics, such as page views, visitor country/region, and device type; (4) email address and inquiry content when users contact us; (5) on-chain transaction information generated or referenced through the Service (such as transaction hash, sender wallet address, recipient wallet address, supported token, supported chain, transfer amount, OpenPay usage fee, payment mode, and payment status); (6) if the user grants camera permission on pages such as /scan for QR code reading, the camera video frames and the decoded QR string; and (7) when the private tip-message feature is used, the message body, sender and recipient wallet addresses, amount, chain ID, transaction hash, and sent time. Some of this information is publicly recorded on the blockchain and may not be deletable or hideable by the Company. To provide the Service's functionality, the Company may store in the user's browser local storage settings related to display and payments, transaction history, payment receipts, wallet connection state, and similar data. Such data is used within the client (the user's device) and is not transmitted to the Company's servers, nor used for cross-site behavioral tracking or advertising. The Company does not use tracking or advertising cookies. For features that involve sign-in (where used), the Company may use session cookies necessary to provide those features. The Company does not collect special-care-required personal information (such as race, creed, social status, medical history, or criminal record). The Company also does not carry out automated decision-making (including profiling) regarding users. Users may delete this client-side data at any time by clearing their browser cache or storage, or by using the deletion features within the Service (such as deleting payment receipts or transaction history). (8) For sellers using the Digital Goods Store, listed product information (title, description, price, receiving wallet address, seller information) and product content (a private URL or text). (9) For buyers, purchase records in the Digital Goods Store (buyer wallet address, product, purchased revision, amount, transaction hash and time of purchase).

section2.title: 2. Purposes of Use
section2.body: We use collected information for: (1) providing, operating, maintaining, and improving the Service; (2) responding to user inquiries; (3) statistical analysis and Service improvement; (4) detecting and preventing fraud, abuse, and unauthorized access; (5) responding to legal obligations; (6) other purposes ancillary to the above; (7) confirming payment status, calculating the OpenPay usage fee, executing gas sponsorship in Gasless Payment mode, detecting fraud, and handling inquiries and incident investigations; (8) camera frames on pages such as /scan are processed entirely within the user's browser to decode the QR code and are never transmitted to the Company's servers or any external destination, nor are they stored. Of the decoded results, only the OpenPay URL category that the Service recognizes (pay / tip / checkout / handle / order / external / eip681 / unknown) is sent to Sentry as an error-observation breadcrumb; the raw QR string and the user's wallet address are not sent to Sentry; and (9) information collected for the private tip-message feature is used solely to display the message to the tip recipient and is not made public. The Company configures its error monitoring not to send personally identifying information, and if unnecessary personal data is nonetheless included in an error log, it will take reasonable measures such as deletion or masking. (10) Product information and product content in the Digital Goods Store are used solely to deliver the product to buyers (post-purchase display and re-access) and are not made public (product content is shown only to buyers). (11) Purchase records are used to show and re-deliver purchased goods to the buyer, to prevent double grants, and as proof of the transaction.

section3.title: 3. Sharing with Third Parties and Service Providers
section3.body: We do not share personal information with third parties without user consent or where required by law. However, we engage the following service providers to operate the Service, all of which we supervise as required by the APPI: - Vercel Inc. sectionShops.title: 3-2. Third-Party Provision of Shop Listing Data (Shops API)
sectionShops.body: When a shop selects “List in AI-agent search” and republishes, the Company provides the listing, based on that shop’s explicit consent, to AI agents and Shops API users for shop search and ordering assistance. Provided fields are the shop @handle, name, tagline, address, ordering mode, dine-in availability, opening and last-order times, minimum pickup lead time, menu item count and price range, supported chains, summaries of accepting status, pause status and sold-out count, the shop page URL, and the menu API URL. Phone numbers are not provided. A shop may withdraw consent at any time by clearing the listing option and republishing; removal from the API normally takes effect within the shared-cache maximum of 60 seconds. On removal, the Shops API listing index and search summary are deleted and are not retained for the purpose of providing the Shops API.

section4.title: 4. Retention Period
section4.body: We retain collected information only for the period necessary to fulfill the purposes of use. Server logs are deleted in sequence 90 days after collection. Inquiry records are deleted 3 years after the last correspondence. On-chain transaction records, by their nature, are permanently public outside our control, and we cannot delete them. Private tip messages are retained for up to 180 days, and the recipient can delete them at any time using “Delete all” on the receiving screen. Product content in the Digital Goods Store is retained while the seller distributes it and as needed to deliver it to buyers, and may be deleted when distribution is stopped by the operator. Purchase records are retained in principle without deletion to preserve buyers' rights (re-access to purchased goods and proof of the transaction).

sectionPush.title: 5. Web Push Notifications (optional)
sectionPush.body: Users may optionally enable push notifications for received payments. Only if enabled, the Company stores in its KV storage the mapping between the user's wallet address and the push subscription endpoint (endpoint and encryption keys) issued by the browser. Up to 5 devices are stored per wallet, the mapping automatically expires after 90 days, and users can delete it at any time by disabling notifications. Notifications are delivered via the push service operated by the browser vendor (such as Apple, Google, or Mozilla). Whether the sale amount is included in the notification body is an optional user setting (off by default); only when turned on does the amount appear on the lock screen and similar surfaces. In logs, the subscription endpoint is recorded as a hash rather than retained in the clear.

sectionSecurity.title: 6. Security Measures for Personal Information
sectionSecurity.body: To prevent the leakage, loss, or damage of acquired personal information and otherwise ensure its safe management, the Company implements necessary and appropriate security measures, including encryption of communications via SSL/TLS, management of access privileges, measures against unauthorized access, and necessary and appropriate supervision of service providers.

section7.title: 7. OpenPay Usage Fee and Gas Sponsorship
section7.body: The OpenPay usage fee is a per-transaction usage fee borne by Merchants who use JPYC gasless payments, as consideration for use of the Service—including payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, supported wallet integration, gas sponsorship and payment relay for JPYC gasless payments, and operation and maintenance of the Service. The OpenPay usage fee is 1% of the payment with a minimum of 2 JPYC (the fee is triggered by JPYC gasless usage, and paths where the Customer pays gas themselves—e.g. USDC via the ERC20 Paymaster—are not in scope). The OpenPay usage fee is taken at the time each payment is executed (at on-chain settlement), split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. The OpenPay usage fee is borne by the Merchant (the Customer pays only the displayed payment amount, and the fee is deducted from the amount the Merchant receives); the net amount the Merchant receives is the payment amount less the OpenPay usage fee. For tips to creators, however, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC per transaction; the 1% of the payment does not apply) is borne by the Customer sending the tip. The principal price of goods and similar amounts (excluding the OpenPay usage fee) continues to be transferred directly to the Merchant's wallet. The OpenPay usage fee is not for the purpose of recovering gas and is not linked to the actual gas amount. Transfers finalized on-chain cannot, by their technical nature, in principle be cancelled, refunded, or modified. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not handle the Network Fee in any way; the Customer pays it from their own wallet, and no OpenPay usage fee arises for this path. However, for JPYC payments checked out via the register (in-store POS) feature, from the July 2026 usage period the same OpenPay usage fee as gasless (1% of the payment) is charged as consideration for use of the Service (the register and other payment systems), even in Standard (with-gas) mode (deducted from the merchant's receipt; the customer still pays their own gas). Payment QR (/pay), tips to creators, the USDC route, and manually created payment links remain out of scope (free). If for any reason the Company cannot collect the OpenPay usage fee, the Company may suspend gasless payment relay for that Merchant, but the act of receiving a payment itself and the use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode remain available. If the rate, calculation method, or collection method of the OpenPay usage fee is changed, the Company will give prior notice. Separately, for the accounting CSV download feature, after this feature is enabled you may purchase a separate optional right to use, the "CSV 24-hour pass" (100 JPYC per purchase, valid for 24 hours from the time of payment). The CSV pass is prepaid; viewing your transaction history and the act of receiving payments remain free. The CSV pass is non-refundable (no refunds or prorated refunds after payment) and does not auto-renew. Re-purchasing grants 24 hours from the new payment time and does not stack onto any remaining time. Paying more than 100 JPYC still grants only 24 hours of validity. Where available in your environment, paying for the CSV pass defaults to gasless purchase (sign only; we bear the blockchain gas required to send it). If you choose the path of buying by sending with gas, the blockchain gas for that transfer is borne by the user. We will announce when this feature becomes available within the Service. In addition, if you use the mobile-order feature (in-store / kiosk ordering and pre-order mobile ordering), the Company applies a different rate of the OpenPay usage fee for use of the mobile-order feature (including the shop page, menu, order management, and order relay): it does not charge this in addition to the gasless usage fee above, but applies only the following rate (this rate is the mobile-order system fee; where the Company sponsors gas for a gasless mobile order, that gas is included in this rate, and the gasless usage fee above is not charged again on top). This fee is charged per mobile-order payment regardless of the payment path (whether gasless or standard, and therefore even for standard payments where the Customer pays the Network Fee themselves); the rate is 1% of the payment for in-store/kiosk and 3% for pre-order mobile ordering. For pre-order mobile ordering, depending on the store setting, either the store bears the fee out of the amount it receives (the Customer pays only the price of goods) or the Customer pays it on top of the price of goods. In either case the principal price of goods is transferred directly to the Merchant's designated wallet (the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales), and only the fee portion is split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. This mobile-order system fee was introduced on June 17, 2026 and applies to use of the mobile-order feature on and after the day the feature becomes available; /pay payment links, tips to creators, and standard payment links other than mobile order are not in scope. In addition, for use of the x402 facilitator operated by the Company (a per-request billing intermediary for APIs and content aimed at AI agents and developers), an x402 facilitator fee of 1% of the payment (1 JPYC minimum; revised 2026-07-05 from the previous 2 JPYC minimum) is added on the buyer's side on top of the listed price (the seller—i.e., the resource registrant—receives the listed amount in full). The Company does not custody sales (non-custodial) and splits only the fee portion (including any gas the Company sponsors) to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. This x402 facilitator fee is a separate consideration, independent of the OpenPay usage fee and the mobile-order system fee above, and applies only to x402 payments (newly established on June 28, 2026). See the Terms of Service and the Specified Commercial Transactions Act notice for details.
